results.description: Ensure SMBv1 protocol is disabled (used by WannaCry/EternalBlue)
results.risk_explanation: SMBv1 is an insecure, legacy protocol vulnerable to remote code execution exploits like EternalBlue (used in the WannaCry ransomware attack). It lacks modern encryption and pre-authentication integrity checks.

results.description: Ensure User Account Control (UAC) is enabled
results.risk_explanation: Disabling UAC allows standard users and processes to silently elevate privileges and modify sensitive system files, registry entries, and core operating system configurations without administrative prompts.

results.description: Ensure RDP requires Network Level Authentication (NLA)
results.risk_explanation: Disabling Network Level Authentication (NLA) allows unauthenticated remote attackers to initiate RDP sessions before presenting credentials, exposing systems to credential brute-forcing, Denial of Service, and unauthenticated RCE exploits (e.g., BlueKeep CVE-2019-0708).

results.description: Ensure Windows Defender Real-Time Protection is active
results.risk_explanation: Disabling Defender real-time protection permits malware execution, malicious memory injections, and script-based droppers to run completely unhindered and undetected.

results.description: Ensure built-in Guest account is disabled
results.risk_explanation: An active Guest account provides anonymous local logon capability and can be leveraged by attackers for initial persistence or reconnaissance on the local network.

results.description: Ensure Windows Firewall is enabled for the Domain profile
results.risk_explanation: Disabling host-based firewalls for domain connections removes the first line of boundary defense against rogue endpoints, lateral network scans, and unauthorized service probing within corporate networks.

results.description: Ensure LSA Protection (RunAsPPL) is enabled to prevent credential dumping
results.risk_explanation: Running the Local Security Authority (LSA) process as a Protected Process Light (PPL) prevents non-protected processes, even those with administrative privileges, from injecting code or dumping credentials (e.g., Mimikatz reading lsass.exe memory).

results.description: Ensure PowerShell script execution policy is restricted
results.risk_explanation: An unrestricted PowerShell execution policy permits execution of unverified, downloaded scripts. Enforcing signed script execution or at least RemoteSigned prevents drive-by or downloaded malicious script execution.
results.remediation_command:
# CIS allows RemoteSigned; AllSigned is stricter but can break local dev scripts
Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope LocalMachine -ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned -Force

results.description: Ensure Automatic Updates are not disabled via policy
results.risk_explanation: Disabling automatic updates prevents timely patching of critical zero-day vulnerabilities and OS security flaws, exposing the platform to known exploits documented in NVD/CVE databases.

results.description: Ensure BitLocker is fully encrypting the system drive (C:)
results.risk_explanation: Unencrypted volumes expose all host data, user credentials, and offline registry hives (SAM, SYSTEM) to physical theft, offline attacks, or malicious live booting.

results.description: Ensure AlwaysInstallElevated is disabled (HKLM) — prevents SYSTEM-level MSI install abuse
results.risk_explanation: When AlwaysInstallElevated is set to 1 in HKLM, Windows Installer executes all MSI packages with NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM privileges, allowing standard unprivileged users to craft a malicious MSI package and immediately gain full root/SYSTEM control.

results.description: Ensure AlwaysInstallElevated is disabled (HKCU)
results.risk_explanation: AlwaysInstallElevated in HKCU must also be 0; if enabled in conjunction with HKLM, standard users can trigger elevated MSI installations from their own user registry hive.

results.description: Ensure WDigest does not cache plaintext credentials in memory
results.risk_explanation: When UseLogonCredential is enabled (1), WDigest retains plaintext passwords in LSASS memory for digest authentication, allowing attackers with administrative access or memory inspection tools to extract cleartext passwords directly.

results.description: Ensure LLMNR (Link-Local Multicast Name Resolution) is disabled to prevent spoofing
results.risk_explanation: LLMNR allows unauthenticated multicast name queries on local subnets. Attackers on the same network use tools like Responder to poison LLMNR responses, tricking victims into sending NTLMv2 password hashes.
results.remediation_command: if (!(Test-Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\DNSClient')) { New-Item -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\DNSClient' -Force }; Set-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\DNSClient' -Name 'EnableMulticast' -Value 0 -Type DWord

results.description: Ensure AutoRun is disabled for all drives
results.risk_explanation: AutoRun / AutoPlay automatically executes programs from newly connected removable media (USB drives, CDs), serving as a common vector for physical and air-gap breaching malware (e.g., Stuxnet).

results.description: Ensure Windows Script Host (wscript/cscript) is disabled
results.risk_explanation: Windows Script Host (WSH) executes VBScript and JScript files (.vbs, .js). It is frequently abused by phishing attachments and initial access payloads to execute malicious code outside browser sandboxes.
results.remediation_command: if (!(Test-Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows Script Host\Settings')) { New-Item -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows Script Host\Settings' -Force }; Set-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows Script Host\Settings' -Name 'Enabled' -Value 0 -Type DWord

results.description: Ensure PowerShell Script Block Logging is enabled
results.risk_explanation: Without Script Block Logging (Event ID 4104), executed PowerShell code—including dynamically de-obfuscated commands and scripts loaded in-memory—is not recorded in event logs, blinding incident responders to malicious activity.

results.description: Ensure built-in Administrator account is disabled
results.risk_explanation: The built-in Administrator account has a well-known SID (RID 500) and is a primary target for password brute-forcing, password spray, and pass-the-hash attacks. It should be disabled in favor of named administrative accounts.

results.description: Ensure SMB client requires security signature
results.risk_explanation: Unsigned SMB traffic is vulnerable to Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) packet tampering and SMB Relay attacks, allowing adversaries to impersonate clients and execute commands on other domain systems.

results.description: Ensure Print Spooler service is stopped on non-print servers (PrintNightmare)
results.risk_explanation: The Windows Print Spooler service has a history of high-severity vulnerabilities (e.g. PrintNightmare CVE-2021-34527 / CVE-2021-1675) allowing remote code execution and local privilege escalation.
results.remediation_command:
# Apply to non-print servers only. If this host requires local printing, leave enabled
Stop-Service -Name Spooler -Force; Set-Service -Name Spooler -StartupType Disabled

results.description: Ensure Credential Guard is enabled via Virtualization-Based Security (VBS)
results.risk_explanation: Credential Guard uses Virtualization-Based Security (VBS) to isolate and protect LSASS secrets (NTLM hashes, Kerberos tickets) inside a secure virtual container, neutralizing Mimikatz memory dumping even from local SYSTEM accounts.

results.description: Ensure LAN Manager (LM) hash storage is disabled in SAM database
results.risk_explanation: LM hashes use weak DES encryption split into two 7-character chunks, allowing trivial brute-forcing with rainbow tables in seconds. Storing LM hashes enables immediate credential recovery from SAM.

results.description: Ensure NTLM authentication minimum protocol is set to NTLMv2 only (refuse LM & NTLM)
results.risk_explanation: Setting LmCompatibilityLevel to 5 enforces 'Send NTLMv2 response only. Refuse LM & NTLM', preventing downgrade attacks, credential relay, and replay attacks on legacy authentication handshakes.

results.description: Ensure anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts and shares is restricted
results.risk_explanation: Allowing anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts allows unauthenticated remote attackers on the local network to query all local usernames, group memberships, and security identifiers (SIDs).

results.description: Ensure the number of cached domain logon credentials is restricted (<= 4)
results.risk_explanation: Windows caches domain logon credentials (mscache/DCC2 hashes) locally in the LSA secrets hive for offline logons. High cache counts leave historical domain password hashes vulnerable to extraction.

results.description: Ensure anonymous access to Named Pipes and Shares is restricted
results.risk_explanation: Null session connections without authentication allow reconnaissance attackers to enumerate IPC$ named pipes, shares, and platform capabilities without providing credentials.

results.description: Ensure UAC elevation prompt for administrators requires credentials on secure desktop
results.risk_explanation: Value 2 requires explicit credentials prompt on the secure desktop, preventing silent UAC bypass attacks (such as DLL hijack or fodhelper auto-elevate) from executing unprompted root actions.

results.description: Ensure UAC elevation prompts for standard users are automatically denied
results.risk_explanation: Setting user consent behavior to 0 automatically denies elevation requests for standard users, preventing social engineering or phishing malware from tricking users into entering admin credentials.

results.description: Ensure UAC Admin Approval Mode is enforced for the built-in Administrator account
results.risk_explanation: By default, the built-in Administrator runs with a full, unfiltered token without UAC oversight. Enabling FilterAdministratorToken strips admin privileges into a standard token until explicitly approved.

results.description: Ensure UAC virtualizes file and registry write failures to per-user locations
results.risk_explanation: Ensures legacy 32-bit applications writing to protected directories (%ProgramFiles%, %SystemRoot%) are redirected to a per-user VirtualStore rather than failing or gaining elevated file handles.

results.description: Ensure UAC switches to the Secure Desktop when prompting for elevation
results.risk_explanation: The Secure Desktop isolates the UAC dialog from the interactive user desktop, preventing malware from using synthetic mouse/keyboard events, clickjacking, or DLL hooks to auto-click 'Yes'.

results.description: Ensure UAC only elevates executables that are signed and validated
results.risk_explanation: Requires all applications requesting administrative elevation to possess a valid, trusted Authenticode cryptographic signature, blocking unverified or tampered binaries from gaining root rights.

results.description: Ensure SMB server requires digital security signatures on all incoming connections
results.risk_explanation: Enforcing SMB server signing blocks SMB Relay attacks (e.g., NTLM relaying via ntlmrelayx), where captured network hashes are forwarded to execute commands on administrative SMB shares (C$, ADMIN$).

results.description: Ensure local accounts with blank passwords are restricted to console logon only
results.risk_explanation: Prevents any local account created with an empty password from logging in remotely via network services (RDP, SMB, WinRM, RPC), mitigating instant remote compromise.

results.description: Ensure Remote Registry service is stopped and disabled
results.risk_explanation: Remote Registry allows remote users to query and modify registry hives over RPC/SMB. Disabling it blocks remote attackers from reading sensitive configuration keys and LSA secrets over the wire.
results.remediation_command: Stop-Service -Name RemoteRegistry -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Set-Service -Name RemoteRegistry -StartupType Disabled -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

results.description: Ensure Windows Remote Management (WinRM) client disables Basic authentication
results.risk_explanation: Basic authentication sends credentials in plaintext (Base64 encoded) across the network. Disabling it enforces Kerberos or Negotiate cryptographic authentication.

results.description: Ensure Windows Remote Management (WinRM) client disallows unencrypted traffic
results.risk_explanation: Allowing unencrypted WinRM traffic allows eavesdroppers on the local network to intercept remote command inputs, executed scripts, and output payloads.

results.description: Ensure Remote Desktop connection encryption level is set to High
results.risk_explanation: Level 3 encrypts all client-to-server and server-to-client packets using 128-bit encryption, protecting keystrokes, clipboard transfers, and displayed screens from sniffing.
results.remediation_command: if (!(Test-Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\Terminal Services')) { New-Item -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\Terminal Services' -Force }; Set-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\Terminal Services' -Name 'MinEncryptionLevel' -Value 3 -Type DWord

results.description: Ensure Microsoft Defender Tamper Protection is enabled
results.risk_explanation: Tamper Protection prevents malicious programs and rootkits from turning off real-time protection, deleting security cloud signatures, or disabling Defender services via registry manipulation.

results.description: Ensure Microsoft Defender Behavioral Monitoring is enabled
results.risk_explanation: Behavioral monitoring analyzes running process heuristics in real-time to intercept zero-day malware and living-off-the-land techniques before signature updates are available.

results.description: Ensure Microsoft Defender scans all downloaded files and attachments (IOAV)
results.risk_explanation: Internet Origin Antivirus (IOAV) scans files downloaded through web browsers and email clients upon arrival, stopping malicious payload drops before execution.

results.description: Ensure Microsoft Defender Cloud Protection (MAPS Reporting) is enabled
results.risk_explanation: MAPS Reporting (Microsoft Active Protection Service) delivers cloud-based AI scanning and real-time intelligence feeds against emerging zero-day threats within milliseconds.

results.description: Ensure Microsoft Defender Potentially Unwanted Application (PUA) blocking is enabled
results.risk_explanation: PUA protection blocks adware, torrent downloaders, coin miners, and bundled surveillance software that introduce secondary vulnerabilities into the operating system.

results.description: Ensure Controlled Folder Access (Anti-Ransomware) is enabled
results.risk_explanation: Controlled Folder Access prevents unauthorized applications from modifying files in protected user directories (Documents, Pictures, Desktop), blocking ransomware file encryption.

results.description: Ensure Virtualization-Based Security (VBS) is enabled
results.risk_explanation: VBS uses hardware virtualization to create a secure memory enclave isolated from the standard Windows kernel, preventing kernel-level exploits from tampering with hypervisor-protected structures.

results.description: Ensure Hypervisor-Protected Code Integrity (HVCI / Memory Integrity) is enabled
results.risk_explanation: HVCI enforces strict code integrity checks inside the secure world before kernel-mode drivers can execute, blocking vulnerable or maliciously signed third-party drivers (BYOVD attacks).

results.description: Ensure PowerShell Module Logging is enabled
results.risk_explanation: Module logging records pipeline execution events and associated invocation data for PowerShell modules (Event ID 4103), tracking administrative cmdlet misuse and attack framework imports.

results.description: Ensure PowerShell Transcription Logging is enabled
results.risk_explanation: Transcription captures all input commands and raw output text into timestamped, append-only text logs on disk, providing complete forensic trails of attacker console sessions.

results.description: Ensure command line process creation auditing is enabled (Event ID 4688 with arguments)
results.risk_explanation: Without full command-line logging, Event ID 4688 records that cmd.exe or powershell.exe ran, but hides the exact arguments, obfuscated flags, or encoded commands passed by the attacker.

results.description: Ensure Windows SmartScreen for File Explorer is enabled
results.risk_explanation: SmartScreen warns users before running unrecognized applications downloaded from the internet (Mark-of-the-Web), blocking malicious droppers and initial access payloads.

attestation_seal.signer: ASArP Platform Root of Trust (TCB-Sealed Key)
